cards.front: What common exercise myth regarding training volume and intensity was challenged by the 1995 CDC/ACSM report?
cards.back: The persistent myth that high volume and high intensity of exercise training (such as jogging 8 km/day or lifting to complete failure) are necessary to attain health-related benefits. The report concluded that substantial health benefits are achieved through a moderate amount of daily physical activity.

cards.front: What moderate physical activity options were highlighted in the landmark 1995 CDC/ACSM consensus report?
cards.back:
Significant health benefits can be obtained by incorporating a moderate amount of physical activity on most, if not all, days of the week, such as:
  • 30 minutes of brisk walking
  • 15 minutes of running
  • 45 minutes of playing volleyball

cards.front: What did research in older adults (aged 70–82 years) demonstrate regarding non-formal physical activity and mortality risk?
cards.back: Research demonstrated that simply being more active greatly reduced the risk of mortality in older adults, independent of participation in a formal structured exercise program.

cards.front: What are the 2007 ACSM/AHA aerobic physical activity recommendations for healthy adults aged 18 to 65 years?
cards.back:
Healthy adults should engage in either:
  • Moderate-intensity aerobic activity: Minimum of 30 minutes on 5 days/week.
  • Vigorous-intensity aerobic activity: Minimum of 20 minutes on 3 days/week.
  • Or an equivalent combination of moderate and vigorous activities.

cards.front: How can the 30-minute daily moderate-intensity aerobic activity recommendation be accumulated throughout the day?
cards.back: Moderate-intensity aerobic activity can be accumulated by performing discrete bouts each lasting ≥ 10 minutes to reach the 30-minute daily total.

cards.front: What is the ACSM/AHA minimum recommendation for maintaining or increasing muscular strength and endurance?
cards.back: Every adult should perform activities that maintain or increase muscular strength and endurance for a minimum of 2 days per week.

cards.front: Why do individuals benefit from exceeding minimum physical activity guidelines?
cards.back: Due to the dose-response relationship between physical activity and health, individuals who exceed minimum recommended amounts derive greater protection against chronic diseases and disabilities, further improve fitness, and prevent unhealthy weight gain.

cards.front: What is the primary objective of the Exercise is Medicine (EIM) initiative launched by the ACSM and AMA?
cards.back: To encourage healthcare providers to routinely assess, counsel, and prescribe physical activity as a standard component of patient medical care, providing education to clinicians in exercise prescription basics.

cards.front: Which clinical resource guide is offered via ExerciseIsMedicine.org to assist healthcare providers?
cards.back: The website provides the 'Health Care Providers' Action Guide' to educate and guide clinicians in including physical activity in their patients' overall healthcare plans.

cards.front: What are the two essential initial steps an individual must take when beginning an exercise program?
cards.back:
The two initial steps are:
  • Step 1: Deciding to take action (behavioral commitment).
  • Step 2: Getting medical clearance through clinical health screening to ensure safe exercise program initiation.
